Bayesian proxy-SVAR with exogeneity, relevance and sign restrictions (Arias-Rubio-Ramirez-Waggoner type)

Source: R/psvar-bayes-full.R
varm_proxy_arw.Rd

Full-likelihood Bayesian proxy-SVAR in the spirit of Arias, Rubio-Ramirez & Waggoner (2021). The r proxies obey the exogeneity restrictions \(E[m_t\varepsilon_{jt}'] = 0\) for the first \(K-r\) shocks and a relevance condition for the last r shocks. As in their Proxy-SVAR (their eq. 3 with the block restrictions), the data have the joint likelihood \(p(Y)\,p(M\mid Y)\) with the proxy equation $$m_t = D y_t + G x_t + \sum_{l=1}^{p_m} H_l m_{t-l} + v_t,\quad v_t\sim N(0,\Upsilon),$$ which the lags of \(y_t\) (and optionally of \(m_t\)) are allowed to enter. The likelihood factorises, so a posterior draw is: \((B,\Sigma)\) from the supplied bvarm() fit (any conjugate prior, e.g. Minnesota) and \((D,G,H,\Upsilon)\) from the first-stage regression (Jeffreys prior), independently. The exogeneity restrictions \(D\Sigma_{tr}q_j=0,\ j\le K-r\), with \(\Sigma=\Sigma_{tr}\Sigma_{tr}'\) and \(Q\) the rotation matrix, are linear in the columns of \(Q\); \(Q\) is drawn column by column from the unit sphere of the admissible subspace (ARW Algorithm 1 / Arias et al. 2018, using the orthogonal-reduced-form parameterisation), and sign restrictions on the impulse responses of the proxy shocks are imposed by accept/reject. With r = 1 the proxy shock is point-identified (\(q_K \propto \Sigma_{tr}'D'\)) and signs only truncate the posterior; with r > 1 exogeneity alone leaves the proxy shocks identified only up to an orthogonal \(r\times r\) rotation, which the sign restrictions (needed for identification) pin down. A reliability truncation \(\lambda_{\min}\{(\Upsilon+D\Sigma D')^{-1}D\Sigma D'\}\ge\gamma\) (ARW 2021 section 2.3, after Caldara & Herbst 2019) is available through reliability.

Usage

varm_proxy_arw(
  fit,
  m,
  target = 1L,
  size = 1,
  signs = NULL,
  reliability = NULL,
  pm = 0L,
  horizon = 20L,
  level = c(0.68, 0.9),
  ndraw = NULL,
  nrot = 1L,
  maxtry = 1000L,
  sign_horizon = 1L
)

id_proxy_bayes(
  fit,
  m,
  target = 1L,
  size = 1,
  signs = NULL,
  reliability = NULL,
  pm = 0L,
  nrot = 1L,
  maxtry = 1000L,
  sign_horizon = 1L
)

Arguments

fit

a bvarm() object (class bvarm).

m

proxy: numeric vector, or T x r matrix of r proxies, aligned with the data (the first p rows are dropped to match the residuals).

target

variable(s) (name or position) whose impact response is normalised to size; length r.

size

impact response of target to each proxy shock (recycled), or NULL for one-standard-deviation shocks (sign normalised so that \(A_0\) has non-negative diagonal; state the sign through signs in that case).

signs

sign restrictions on the responses of the proxy shocks: K x r matrix (or K x r x H array) of +1, -1, 0; column i is the i-th proxy shock (shock K - r + i). NULL for none. The sign of a shock is otherwise normalised by size (impact on target).

reliability

minimum reliability \(\gamma\in[0,1)\); draws below are discarded (truncated prior).

pm

number of lags of the proxy in the first-stage regression.

horizon

maximum horizon (impact is 0).

level

confidence levels; bands are equal-tailed percentiles.

ndraw

number of posterior draws to use (default: all stored draws).

nrot

accepted rotations kept per reduced-form draw.

maxtry

maximum rotation draws per reduced-form draw.

sign_horizon

number of horizons (from impact) over which a matrix signs is imposed.

Value

varm_proxy_arw(): a varm_proxy object (method = "arw") with estimate (posterior median), draws, bands, plus accept_rate, reliability (posterior median of the reliability index, per proxy). id_proxy_bayes(): a varm_id for irf() on a bvarm() fit (columns of non-proxy shocks are zero).

Details

What is and is not the ARW posterior. The prior implied is the conjugate prior on the reduced form times the (conditionally) uniform prior on the admissible rotations, with importance weights set to one. ARW's Algorithm 2 instead targets a normal-generalised-normal prior on the structural parameters and re-weights draws by a volume element (their Theorem 3, taken from Arias et al. 2018); that element is not given in the paper and is not implemented here. The two posteriors coincide when the proxy shocks are point-identified (r = 1, no sign restrictions on non-proxy shocks) up to the reduced-form prior; with r > 1 they differ through the prior on the rotation. Non-proxy shocks are not identified and their IRF columns are returned as zero. Compare varm_proxy_bayes(), which does not allow lags of \(y_t\) in the proxy equation and has no sign or reliability restrictions, and varm_proxy_gkr() for prior-robust inference when r > 1 or shocks other than the proxy shocks are of interest.

Not implemented: Caldara & Herbst (2019)'s Metropolis-within-Gibbs sampler with a structural measurement equation \(m_t=\beta\varepsilon_{1t}+\sigma_\nu\nu_t\) (where the proxy likelihood depends on \((B,\Sigma)\) through \(u_t\), so the proxy updates the VAR coefficients) and priors on \(\beta,\sigma_\nu\).

References

Arias, J. E., Rubio-Ramirez, J. F. and Waggoner, D. F. (2021). Inference in Bayesian proxy-SVARs. Journal of Econometrics 225(1), 88-106.

Arias, J. E., Rubio-Ramirez, J. F. and Waggoner, D. F. (2018). Inference based on SVARs identified with sign and zero restrictions. Econometrica 86(2), 685-720.

Caldara, D. and Herbst, E. (2019). Monetary policy, real activity, and credit spreads: evidence from Bayesian proxy SVARs. AEJ: Macroeconomics 11(1), 157-192.

See also

varm_proxy_gkr(), varm_proxy_bayes(), varm_proxy()

Examples

# \donttest{
set.seed(1)
e <- matrix(rnorm(900), 300)
y <- matrix(0, 300, 3)
for (t in 2:300) y[t, ] <- 0.4 * y[t - 1, ] + e[t, ] %*% t(matrix(c(1, .3, .2, 0, 1, .4, .5, .2, 1), 3))
bf <- bvarm(y, p = 1, ndraw = 300, nburn = 100)
varm_proxy_arw(bf, m = e[, 3] + rnorm(300, sd = 0.5), target = 3, horizon = 8)
#> <varm_proxy> shock to y3 (size 1), horizon 0..8, 300 posterior draws
# }
